---
title: "Coding Conventions"
order: 4
---

### C1 — Auto-formatter per language

No human should format code. Hand formatting to a tool so nobody burns a review comment on whitespace. Consistent style also keeps diffs focused on real changes instead of reflows.

```bash
black src/                          # Python
Rscript -e 'styler::style_dir("R")'  # R
shfmt -w scripts/                   # Shell
```

### C2 — Descriptive names beat comments that explain bad names

A good name never goes stale. subject_reaction_times explains itself. srt needs a comment, and that comment drifts from the code the moment someone edits nearby.

```python
# bad
srt = df[df.srt > 0.1]
# good
valid = trials[trials.reaction_time > 0.1]
```

### C3 — No hard-coded absolute paths

/Users/alice/ breaks for everyone else. Absolute paths fail the instant a second person runs the code. Use relative paths or one path variable at the top so the project moves between machines.

```python
# bad
df = pd.read_csv("/Users/alice/data/rt.csv")
# good
from pathlib import Path
DATA = Path(__file__).parent / "data"
df = pd.read_csv(DATA / "rt.csv")
```

### C4 — Functions for anything used more than twice

Fix it once, not in five places. Copy, paste, tweak, and now four near-copies drift apart. Pull anything you write a third time into one function so a fix lands everywhere at once.

```python
def zscore(x):
    return (x - x.mean()) / x.std()

rt_z  = zscore(df.rt)
amp_z = zscore(df.amp)
```

### C5 — Config at the top, not scattered

Changing a run should take one edit. Keep parameters, paths, and thresholds in one block or file instead of sprinkled through the code. Tuning an experiment then means editing one spot.

```python
# config.py
RAW    = "data/raw.csv"
RT_MIN = 0.1
N_BOOT = 10_000
```
